result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_navigable_small_world_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add Kleinberg's navigable small-world graph: a grid with long-range links. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_navigable_small_world_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add Kleinberg's navigable small-world graph: a grid with long-range links. title: >- [Graph.add_navigable_small_world_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add Kleinberg's navigable small-world graph: a grid with long-range links. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add Kleinberg's navigable small-world graph: a grid with long-range links. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12633-L12772){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_navigable_small_world_graph( n, p=1, q=1, r=2.0, dim=2, seed=None, pos_attr="pos", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Navigable small-world graph](/assets/graphs/add-navigable-small-world-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three navigable small-world graphs on a 3 by 3 grid with p=1 and r=2, for q=0, 1, and 2 long-range contacts per node. At q=0 it is just the grid; each node then adds q contacts chosen with probability falling off as the squared grid distance, so most land on neighbors already joined, and the accent edges are the ones that reach farther: 1 at q=1 and 5 at q=2. Some bow to clear the nodes they would pass through." width="100%"} Arranges `n ** dim` nodes in an `n` by `n` grid (or its analogue in `dim` dimensions). Each node links to every node within lattice distance `p` (the Manhattan distance on the grid), plus `q` long-range contacts, each chosen with probability proportional to `d ** -r` where `d` is the lattice distance. Kleinberg showed that with `r` equal to `dim`, greedy routing that only knows grid positions finds short paths, in a number of steps polynomial in `log(n)`; for any other `r` it needs a power of `n`. The process follows NetworkX's `navigable_small_world_graph()`, which can occasionally draw a node as its own contact through an indexing slip; here a contact is always another node. Each node's grid coordinates are stored as a list of `dim` integers in the `pos_attr=` node attribute, and the nodes are created in lexicographic order of their coordinates. The links are directed: each node's own contacts. A directed graph keeps them as they are, with each lattice link present in both directions. In an undirected graph the two directions of a link become a single edge. Either way, a long-range contact that repeats an existing link is not added again. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Navigable small-world graphs are useful for: - studying decentralized search and greedy routing - modeling social networks, where most ties are local and a few are long-range - testing how the distance exponent `r=` changes path lengths and navigability ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes along each side of the grid, so `n ** dim` nodes in all (at most `1,000,000`; building takes time proportional to the square of the node count). [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Lattice distance within which every pair of nodes is linked. Default is `1`, the grid's nearest neighbors. Must be at least `1`. [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of long-range contacts per node. Default is `1`. [r]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Exponent of the distance decay for long-range contacts. Default is `2.0`. Must be non-negative; `0` makes the contacts uniform. [dim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of grid dimensions. Default is `2`. Must be at least `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [pos_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pos"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's grid coordinates. Default is `"pos"`. Pass `None` to skip storing them. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` or `q=` is negative, `p=` or `dim=` is less than `1`, `r=` is negative, or `n ** dim` is more than `1,000,000`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A `10` by `10` directed grid with one long-range contact per node: ::: {#bca3f99a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_navigable_small_world_graph(n=10, seed=1) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 418) ``` ::: ::: The grid coordinates are stored on the nodes, row by row: ::: {#55dc2736 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [graph.get_node_attrs("pos")[v] for v in (1, 2, 11, 100)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [9, 9]] ``` ::: ::: With `r=0` the long-range contacts are spread uniformly and shorten paths the most; with a large `r` they stay near home, and the diameter approaches the bare grid's `18`: ::: {#98540eb5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ ( r, ec.Graph() .add_navigable_small_world_graph(n=10, r=r, seed=1) .get_diameter(), ) for r in (0.0, 2.0, 6.0) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [(0.0, 5), (2.0, 8), (6.0, 16)] ``` ::: :::
